audit.name: CyberLite synthesis-calibration contamination, deduplication and split-integrity audit
audit.status: no_threshold_violations; one field-level duplication finding and coverage gaps reported
audit.independence: Exact hash, SimHash, MinHash/Jaccard, 13-gram and group-split methods were reimplemented standalone and cross-checked against cyberlite.data.cleaning, contamination, semantic and splits; both implementations agree.

minhash.verification: exact Jaccard over 5-word shingle sets for every pair (no LSH sampling)

paraphrase_heuristic.method: token-set Jaccard (prompt vs benchmark question; response vs question+choices+answer) and symmetric containment; no stemming or embeddings
paraphrase_heuristic.maxima_note: Each maximum is taken over benchmark items independently for that field; a prompt maximum and a response maximum may come from different items.
paraphrase_heuristic.interpretation: No record exceeds Jaccard 0.5. The containment flags come from short benchmark questions or answers being subsets of longer prompts/responses; directed prompt-in-benchmark never exceeds 0.44. This is a heuristic, not proof of no paraphrase leakage.

findings.summary: One validation record shares an 819-character response byte-for-byte with nine train records in the NVD CPE-applicability family.
findings.evidence: grnd-nist-nvd-nist-nvd-00b3cc38194e31f8-applicability (validation, CVE-2020-29504) versus nine train *-applicability records; response-field identity 1.0; whole-record Jaccard 0.535, below the 0.88 threshold, so whole-record dedup did not remove it.
findings.action: Deduplicate on the response field, or drop/regenerate the affected validation item, before using validation loss as an early-stopping signal.

findings.summary: Several task families are dominated by a single prompt skeleton.
findings.evidence: evidence-grounded-qa 41/41 (100%), false-positive-recognition 10/10 (100%), uncertainty-handling 9/9 (100%), attack-technique-recognition 4/4 (100%), structured-json 27/30 (90%), command-explanation 42/47 (89.4%). Global top skeleton is 8.66% (42/485); top five 27.84%.
findings.action: Add paraphrase-diverse prompt variants per family and report per-family results rather than only aggregate scores.

findings.summary: CyberSecEval is not available locally, so it was not screened.
findings.evidence: Only benchmarks/cyberseceval/README.md exists; no JSONL under data/evaluation and no entry in the build's benchmark index.
findings.action: Obtain a license-compliant copy and rerun the screen. Do not describe the corpus as CyberSecEval-clean.

findings.summary: The closest MinHash pair is 0.8555, only 0.0245 below the 0.88 threshold, and one pair is above 0.80.
findings.evidence: grnd-openssh-docs-openssh-docs-841d94ec4f1d6d22-requirement-1 and -requirement-2, both train and same group. No pair reaches 0.88, so the configured threshold passes.
findings.action: Keep the threshold; recheck after template or source updates. If the threshold is relaxed to 0.85, this same-group pair would be removed.

findings.summary: Within-corpus SimHash minimum distance is 4 bits against a 3-bit threshold; cross-split minimum is 6 bits.
findings.evidence: Six pairs at distance 4 (five train, one validation), 13 at distance 5, 17 at distance 6; no pair at <=3 and none at <=5 across splits.
findings.action: Keep threshold 3; review if the corpus grows substantially.

findings.summary: The committed deduplication_report.json describes the 1,999-record candidate pool (1,960 kept; 5 semantic and 34 SimHash removals), not the final 500-record calibration corpus.
findings.evidence: Candidate-stage report versus independent final-corpus recount: 0 exact, 0 SimHash <=3, 0 MinHash >=0.88.
findings.action: Label the report's pipeline stage explicitly so readers do not compare it with final-corpus counts.

findings.summary: The three authored evaluation suites exist both under data/evaluation and data/synthesis/eval_authored with identical content.
findings.evidence: e1/e2/e3 SHA-256 values match cyberlite_eval_factual_v1, cyberlite_eval_vulnerability_v1 and cyberlite_eval_logs_ir_v1. The build scanned the data/evaluation copies, so the earlier coverage gap is closed.
findings.action: Keep one canonical copy (or add a checksum guard) to prevent drift.

conclusion.deduplication: No exact, SimHash (<=3) or MinHash (>=0.88) duplicates in the 500-record corpus. The closest MinHash pair is 0.8555 (0.0245 below threshold); the closest SimHash pair is 4 bits (1 bit above threshold).
conclusion.leakage: No whole-record cross-split leakage and no metadata.group in more than one split. One validation response is byte-identical to nine train responses (F1). The closest whole-record cross-split pair is 0.535.
conclusion.contamination: 0 of 500 records were removed at 13-gram/0.20 across six available evaluation files. Maximum overlap is 4.19%, from shared CVSS vector strings and upstream CWE/ATT&CK definitions. CyberSecEval was not screened.
conclusion.templates: Prompt diversity is the main concentration risk: 307 skeletons for 485 prompts, but seven families use one skeleton for 89-100% of their records.

limitations: All duplicate and contamination checks are lexical. Paraphrase, translation and conceptual overlap are not detected; an empty finding is not proof of absence.
MinHash used 128 permutations over 5-word shingles and exact Jaccard for all 124,750 pairs, so LSH sampling cannot hide a pair in this corpus. It still cannot recognize semantic equivalence.
13-gram fingerprints require at least 13 words. All 500 records qualified, but benchmark items shorter than 13 words contribute no fingerprints; paraphrase was screened separately.

The paraphrase heuristic is token-set Jaccard/containment without stemming, synonyms or embeddings. Symmetric containment over-fires when a short benchmark question or answer is a subset of a long prompt or response.
The audit covers train/validation/test only; preferences.jsonl, quarantine.jsonl and review batches were not in scope.
No record has human_reviewed=true; automated screening is not human review.
CyberSecEval and any other absent benchmark were not screened; absence is not a pass.
Field-level duplicate detection used the exact response field; it does not detect near-identical responses below the whole-record threshold.
The candidate-stage deduplication report (1,999 inputs) and the final-corpus recount (500 records) describe different populations.
Counts describe build cyberlite-syn-2.0.0-04a21fdaa5ec and must be recomputed after any data change.
